input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 is the only liquidated-damages mechanic in the document and it runs against us: a late invoice triggers fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, expressly framed as liquidated damages. That is not an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, so it fails the fallback, and because a minor payment delay can compound past the remaining contract value it sits in walk-away territory. We propose the preferred position: delete the charge and state unconditionally that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us. No other clause retains a formula or payment mechanic dependent on § 7.7 (§ 7.3 only restricts Vendor from charging interest on amounts not due).

ops.oldText: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: 7.7 Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the late-payment liquidated damages charge of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, which our playbook does not accept, and replaced it with a clear statement that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us. If a liquidated amount is unavoidable, we can accept a sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages in § 7.7 and confirm no LDs or penalties payable by Customer.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
